valuation_philosophy: Docebo is valued on a FCF-growth DCF using FY2025 FCF of $38.4M as the base. Shareholders' equity is excluded as an anchor because the balance sheet turned negative after the $60M SIB and $61M 365Talents acquisition (both largely debt-financed), making book value uninformative for intrinsic value. EPS CAGRs are also excluded as an anchor because they swung violently during the profitability ramp (0.08 -> 0.86 -> 1.28 diluted EPS in three years). The FCF margin expansion thesis (15.8% in FY2025 -> 20-25% over 5 years) anchors all three scenarios. Revenue growth rates are cross-checked against FY2026 guidance ($271-273M, implying ~12% growth) and the structural ARR trajectory ex-OEM headwinds.

inputs.note: Net Debt = Total Debt $79.1M - Cash $63.2M = $15.9M (Docebo is modestly net-indebted post-SIB and 365Talents acquisition). Shares outstanding reduced from 30.3M (FY2023) to 25.7M (Q1-2026) via $60M SIB at $20.40 and ongoing NCIB.

market_data.note: FY2026E uses guidance midpoint: revenue $272M, Adj. EBITDA $55.5M. FCF estimated at ~$47M (guidance EBITDA * ~85% cash conversion, consistent with FY2025 FCF/EBITDA ratio of 87%).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders equity turned negative ($(0.6M) at Q1-2026) after the $60M SIB and $61M 365Talents acquisition were largely debt-financed; equity CAGR is therefore not usable as a growth anchor. EPS CAGR of 300% reflects profitability ramp from near-zero, not a sustainable forward rate. FCF growth rates are used as the primary anchor, with revenue growth as the guardrail (11.9% FY2025 actual, guidance ~12% for FY2026).
historical_growth.note_on_3yr_5yr: Only 3 clean annual data points available (FY2022, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025). FCF was negligible in FY2022 ($0.8M), so 3-yr FCF CAGR is unusable. Revenue 3yr CAGR of 19.1% reflects faster early growth; the business has decelerated to ~12% as it scales.

base.description: In line with FY2026 guidance ($271-273M revenue, $54.5-56.5M Adj. EBITDA = ~20% margin). FCF margin expands from 15.8% to ~20% by Y5 as operating leverage materialises. Revenue growth decelerates from 12% toward 8% over 5 years as ARR base grows. Net debt of $15.9M is repaid from FCF within 1 year. No credit for $1M+ enterprise wins (consistent with management guidance conservatism). OEM headwind assumed fully absorbed by FY2026.

bull.description: Multi-product AI platform (365Talents + Zive + AgentHub + MCP) drives ACV expansion and NDRR recovery. FedRAMP wins add $10-20M ARR by FY2027. FCF margin expands to 25% as R&D efficiency improves and acquisition integration completes. ACV growth sustains at 15-20% annually. Share buybacks continue at NCIB pace.

bear.description: Competition from bundled HCM suites (SAP/Workday/Microsoft) intensifies. NDRR declines below 97% as OEM wind-down and SMB churn exceed new logo growth. 365Talents integration fails to deliver cross-sell revenue. FCF margin stagnates near 16-17% due to ongoing restructuring costs and AI API expenses. Leverage constrains flexibility.

entry_price.methodology: Price to achieve 15% IRR from today to terminal value (5 years): entry = TV_per_share / (1.15)^5

base.note: Entry price of $20.26 is 15.6% above current price, meaning the stock is already near or below the 15% CAGR entry threshold in the base case.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC (8.5% to 12.5%), Columns = Terminal Growth Rate (1.5% to 3.5%). All values are intrinsic value per share in USD, using base case FCF growth rates.

probability_weighted.rationale: Base weighted at 55%: guidance raised, profitability proven, FCF growing. Bear weighted at 25%: leveraged balance sheet, integration risk, competitive pressure from suite vendors are real. Bull at 20%: multi-product platform and FedRAMP optionality are real but not yet revenue-generating at scale.

checks_run.note: 3.2x is squarely within the range for profitable SaaS growing at 10-15%. Docebo's current market price (1.7x) is below the low end of this range, suggesting the market is pricing in material execution failure.

15.7x is reasonable for a company with 20%+ EBITDA margins and 12% revenue growth. Docebo traded at 25.5x EV/EBITDA as recently as January 2026 (at $40/share). Bear case implies only 8.9x EV/EBITDA, consistent with distressed or no-growth SaaS.
18.2x is at the lower end of the peer range, reflecting conservative FCF estimate (~$47M estimated for FY2026 vs $43.9M Adj EBITDA guidance of $55.5M, implying 15.8% FCF/Rev ratio).

Current market price implies trough multiples equivalent to a no-growth business. The gap between current price ($17.52) and base IV ($33.33) represents the discount the market is applying, likely due to: (1) leveraged balance sheet post-SIB + acquisitions, (2) near-zero GAAP equity creating balance sheet concern, (3) integration execution risk from 365Talents and Zive, (4) small/mid-cap SaaS de-rating since 2022.

investment_thesis.recommendation: UNDERVALUED - High Conviction at Current Price
investment_thesis.risk_reward_ratio: ~90% upside to base case vs ~6% downside to bear case at current price
investment_thesis.key_insight: At $17.52, Docebo trades at 1.7x forward revenue and 8.4x forward EBITDA with 12% organic revenue growth, 20% EBITDA margins, and an AI-native multi-product platform strategy. The SIB at $20.40 (completed March 2026) was management buying stock at a 17% premium to today's price. The current valuation implies the market expects near-zero terminal growth or imminent business impairment, neither of which is supported by the operating data.

365Talents cross-sell to existing 3,500+ customer base demonstrates NDRR recovery above 100%
AgentHub and MCP Server GA (July-Fall 2026) generate measurable new ARR
ARR ex-OEM sustains 13-15% growth confirming underlying acceleration
Continued NCIB reduces share count further, amplifying per-share value
bear_case_triggers: ARR growth decelerates below 8% (below market growth rate) indicating competitive losses
NDRR falls materially below 99%, signaling accelerating churn
365Talents integration costs persist beyond FY2026 with no cross-sell traction
Credit facility covenants breached or lenders reduce revolver capacity

Net Dollar Retention Rate (FY2025: 99%; need to stabilize or recover toward 102%+)
ACV growth (Q1-2026: $71K, +25.9% YoY; need to sustain >$70K)
Adj. EBITDA margin progress vs FY2026 guidance of 20.1-20.7%

methodology_notes.fcf_approach: FCF-based DCF using FY2025 FCF of $38.4M as base year. FCF growth rates calibrated against: (1) revenue guidance ~12% for FY2026, (2) EBITDA margin expansion from 18.1% to 20%+ per guidance, (3) FCF/EBITDA conversion ratio of ~87% (FY2025: 38.4/43.9). Bear case FCF growth at 4-12% vs revenue growth implies stable FCF margins. Bull case growth at 14-28% implies FCF margin expansion to 25%.
methodology_notes.wacc_calculation: Base 10.5%: risk-free rate ~4.5% (10Y UST), equity risk premium 5.5%, beta 1.1x (profitable, growing SaaS with moderate leverage). Bull 9.5%: lower risk as platform strategy de-risks terminal value. Bear 12.0%: elevated WACC reflects balance sheet leverage and integration execution risk.
methodology_notes.terminal_growth: Base 2.5% reflects long-run GDP-adjacent growth for enterprise SaaS with mission-critical compliance and training use cases. Bull 3.0% reflects AI-platform optionality. Bear 2.0% reflects stagnation risk.
methodology_notes.net_debt_treatment: Net Debt of $15.9M (Total Debt $79.1M - Cash $63.2M) subtracted from Enterprise Value. The gross debt represents the NBC credit facility drawdown to finance the $60M SIB and $61M 365Talents acquisition. This is appropriate leverage for a business generating $38-55M of FCF annually.
methodology_notes.shares_outstanding: Uses Q1-2026 diluted shares of 25.7M. Reduced from 30.3M at FY2023 peak through NCIB + $60M SIB. Ongoing NCIB of up to 1.27M shares through May 2027 will further reduce count, providing modest additional per-share uplift not modelled.
